points.reason: A bus write satisfying the strobe, address and selection conditions at line 44 assigns the selected lock bit at line 45, allowing unauthorized state changes or persistent lock assertion.
The address-derived sel at line 51 chooses the lock affected by the write at lines 44-45, so a crafted address can corrupt the intended lock or leave it unavailable.
This process only produces the registered lock-status readback and does not modify or block the internal lock state; confidentiality is not an objective for this concept.
bus_req_i.addr directly generates sel at line 51, which selects the lock updated at line 44 and the lock data returned at line 68, allowing a crafted address to redirect the access.
The spinlock process consumes sel to update lock_q but does not alter, expose or block the selection itself.
The response process uses sel in a lock-status computation but does not modify or block the selection, and confidentiality is not an objective for this concept.
